correctness.rationale: For all integers m,n >= 3, assume m <= n and use d(s,u) as the sum of forward modular increments. Every y-row needs a landmark from the ordered pair (i,j) against (i,j-1). For p=(a-1,j), q=(a,j-1), the possible differences d(s,q)-d(s,p) are 0,-m,n,n-m; since n>=m, only a landmark in x-column a with y!=j makes q closer than p. Thus every x-column needs two landmarks: |S| >= max(n,2m). The proved interval-expansion lemma certifies all ordered pairs using the exact modular distance-difference identity and split cases Delta+delta<=m and >m. Explicit sets of sizes n when n>=2m and 2m when m<=n<2m satisfy expansion; swapping coordinates completes all m,n. One source-free pure Python checker directly tested 83 cases; an independent MILP checker proved 10 finite optima. No finite test is used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full-text product theorem in arXiv:2610.35041v1 requires source-containing cycle factors and expressly excludes source-free consistently directed cycles (Theorem 6.4, Remark 6.5). The present max{max(m,n),2min(m,n)} formula is instead proved by column/row lower obstructions and cyclic interval expansion. Older ordinary and strong metric dimensions use different predicates and do not imply the solid ordered-pair result. Four targeted mathematical-record queries and public searches using equivalent directed torus, Cartesian product, source-free, and metric terminology yielded no covering claim. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a uniqueness certificate; the residual historical-priority risk is explicit.

value.rationale: The sharp two-parameter solid dimension of source-free directed cycle products answers a natural omission explicitly highlighted by Remark 6.5 of the motivating primary paper. Neither the earlier forced-vertex product formula nor ordinary/strong metric dimension yields it. The transition between n and 2m, the local obstruction, and interval-expanding constructions are structural contributions for an infinite vertex-transitive family with no forced vertices. The exact natural graph invariant is motivated independently of computational experimentation.
